test_title: PYST 52: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 11 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A shopkeeper, on the eve of Diwali, allowed a series of discounts on television sets. Find the selling price of a television set, if the marked price of television is ₹1,200 and successive discounts are 15% and 10%.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price (SP) can be calculated directly by multiplying the Marked Price with successive discount factors.

SP = MP × (100 − D₁)/100 × (100 − D₂)/100

SP = 1200 × (85/100) × (90/100)

SP = 1200 × 0.85 × 0.9 = 918

**∴ The correct answer is ₹918.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹1200

Successive discounts = 15% and 10%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20d49ddc74a322ad891c839341afe85323c618eba2e7e843a5b3f89bdecca736.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 1200 − (15/100 × 1200)

⇒ Price = 1200 − 180 = ₹1020

⇒ SP after 2nd discount = 1020 − (10/100 × 1020)

⇒ SP = 1020 − 102 = ₹918

**∴ The correct answer is ₹918.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Discount Formula

When two successive discounts of A% and B% are given, the equivalent single discount can be directly determined using: D = (A + B − A×B/100)%.

Relation between MP, CP, Profit%, and Discount%

The exact ratio of Marked Price (MP) to Cost Price (CP) when a certain profit is made after giving a discount is: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%).

Buy X Get Y Free Discount

In scenarios involving free items, the net percentage discount is computed as: Discount % = [Y ÷ (X + Y)] × 100.
